title: Longest Run Without Repeats
statement:
Given a string s, return the length of the longest stretch of consecutive characters in which no character appears twice.

A stretch must be contiguous: you may not skip characters.

examples.why: "ploy-dev" has eight different characters. Any longer stretch contains both "d"s or both "e"s.
Every stretch longer than one character repeats "a".
"mzuxt" is the longest stretch. The string has six different letters, but no stretch holds all of them.

constraints: s holds printable ASCII characters, including spaces
hints: Checking every substring is O(n²) substrings, each with its own repeat check. What work is repeated between neighbouring substrings?
Keep a window [start, i] that never contains a repeat. When s[i] is already inside the window, the window's start has to move.
Remember the last index where you saw each character. If that index is inside the window, jump start to one past it — never move start backwards.

explain.intuition: Any answer is a window [start, i] with no repeats. Walk i left to right and keep the longest valid window that ends at i. When s[i] already appears in the window, everything up to and including that earlier copy has to leave — so start jumps to one past it.
steps: Keep a map from character to the last index where you saw it, a start pointer at 0, and best = 0.
For each index i: look up the last index of s[i]. If it exists and is ≥ start, it is inside the window, so set start = last + 1.
Record i as the new last index of s[i].
The window [start, i] has no repeats now; update best with its length i - start + 1.
pitfalls: Moving start backwards. In "abba", the second a was last seen at 0, which is already outside the window (start is 2). Only jump when the old index is ≥ start.
Forgetting the empty string: the answer is 0, not 1.

complexity.space: O(k), k = number of distinct characters

solutions.title: Check every start
solutions.idea: For each start index, extend to the right with a set until a character repeats. Simple and correct, but each start rescans characters the previous start already saw.

solutions.title: Sliding window with last-seen index
solutions.idea: One pass. The window start only moves forward, jumping straight past the earlier copy of a repeated character.

followups: Return the substring itself, not just its length.
Allow at most k repeats of any character inside the window. What changes?
